junction.name: Delancey Street & Essex Street, New York City

claims.text: Delancey Street & Essex Street had 39 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 17 pedestrians injured, 7 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Delancey Street & Essex Street's own: the city's record places 107 of the 251 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.7 million a year.
51% of crashes here happened at night (7 pm to 6 am), against 36% at the city's priority junctions.
15% of crashes here involved a taxi or for-hire car, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: no one hurt and a taxi or for-hire car was involved in 13% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 3% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead and a taxi or for-hire car was involved in 14% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 4% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $401,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.6 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $208,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Delancey Street, Essex Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 1, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 3.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 1, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 3
Subject: Request for safety study at Delancey Street & Essex Street – 86 crashes in 5 years

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write about Delancey Street & Essex Street to request a safety study and timely fixes on the roads you are responsible for: Delancey Street and Essex Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 86 crashes, including 39 injury crashes. People injured include 17 pedestrians and 7 cyclists. No one was killed in this period. This is a city priority location. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is about $2.7 million per year. The record shows no safety work in the period. The last recorded treatment was a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2008.

We ask you to assess on site:

- reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders), FHWA-cited, expected to prevent about 1.2 injury crashes per year (about $401,000 in harm avoided per year) and to pay for itself if it costs less than about $2.8 million.

- longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals), subject to a site check, expected to prevent about 0.6 injury crashes per year (about $208,000 in harm avoided per year) and to pay for itself if it costs less than about $1.5 million. Please check first whether the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Thank you for considering safety improvements at this junction.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
